programs.title: Agents on the Shop Floor: Understanding Agent-Managed Workplaces at Lou Gehrig's Bronx
programs.grade_or_level: Adult learners, union members and stewards
outcomes: Explain how an agent-managed, human-governed DAO keeps decisions like votes and treasury transfers in human hands
Read real map and service data around Yankee Stadium to identify community assets and risks
Draft a mock proposal for the Proposal Forum using agent-prepared drafts
Practice collective governance using the DAO's reserved-for-humans rules

sessions.activity: Study the ALS DAO charter and the six human-reserved actions; map which decisions members, not agents, must make in a workplace context.
Use the Evidence Monitor workflow on the local map square (578 buildings, 50 parks, Lou Gehrig Plaza) to summarize neighborhood facts without inventing statistics.
Small groups draft a benefit-fund proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter role simulated; members debate and vote — the enactment step stays human.
Define measurable outcomes for the drafted proposal and set up simple tracking the Progress Tracker role would maintain between decision cycles.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized session feedback, proposal drafts stripped of names, and aggregated voting-pattern summaries to improve shared agent-drafting templates. No personal or employer data is collected.
programs.consent: Participation is voluntary with opt-in at enrollment; consent explained in plain language and by shop stewards; anyone may withdraw and have contributions deleted; no individually identifying data leaves the room.

programs.title: Iron Horse Stewards: Kids Explore Lou Gehrig's Bronx with AI Helpers
outcomes: Connect Lou Gehrig, ALS, and Yankee Stadium's Harlem River setting to why communities organize for public good
Distinguish what AI agents may do versus what people must decide
Read a real neighborhood map and count land features accurately
Build a simple mock proposal as a class

sessions.activity: Learn the DAO mission — AI as a public good — and sort decision cards into 'agent can prepare' and 'only people decide' piles.
Explore the real map square: find Joyce Kilmer Park, Mill Pond Park, Taqwa Community Farm and the Harlem River; record only true counts from the map data.
Class drafts a park-improvement idea for Lou Gehrig Plaza with an agent-style draft; students debate and hold the final vote themselves.
Create a poster or chart tracking the class proposal's outcomes, mirroring the Progress Tracker role.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized, aggregated classroom artifacts (map worksheets and proposal text with all names removed) contributed to shared curriculum examples for other classrooms.
programs.consent: Written guardian/parent consent required before participation, plus student assent; no photos, names, or identifiable work shared; guardians may withdraw consent at any time and contributions are removed from shared models.

programs.title: Evidence-First Advocacy: Running Agent-Supported Research in the Bronx Square
programs.grade_or_level: Professional staff, program managers and field researchers
outcomes: Apply the agent-managed DAO workflow (monitor, synthesize, scout, route, draft, track) to an advocacy project
Ground claims strictly in real map facts and cited sources, avoiding invented statistics
Design measurable outcomes and a progress-tracking plan
Prepare a funding-ready proposal draft for human decision-makers

sessions.activity: Practice evidence synthesis using the world's actual sources and the 1200m square's named places; every claim must cite the map or brief.
Simulate Task Router and Collaborator Scout roles to build a working group around Bronx sites like the Andrew Freedman Home and Bronx Terminal Market area.
Draft a grant proposal with agent-style preparation, peer review it, and route final enactment decisions to designated human stewards.
Build an outcomes dashboard template tied to charter-style measurable outcomes, with update cadence between decision cycles.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized methodology notes, redacted proposal templates, and aggregated evaluation results shared to improve open agent-workflow toolkits for the sector.
programs.consent: Staff opt in via organizational data-sharing agreement; individual contributions anonymized and aggregated; withdrawal honored at any time; no beneficiary or partner data shared without separate consent.

programs.title: Governance by People, Work by Agents: A Board-Level Workshop
programs.grade_or_level: Board members, executive directors and nonprofit governance teams
outcomes: Articulate the 'Agents operate; people govern' model and its six human-reserved actions
Assess which nonprofit decisions should never be delegated to agents
Run a mock decision cycle from agent-drafted proposal to human vote
Set charter-style measurable outcomes for a mission program

sessions.activity: Map the organization's own decisions onto the reserved-for-humans list (final vote, amend, transfer, enact, distribute, appoint); discuss why each stays human.
Board receives an agent-style draft proposal, debates it, and executes the final vote — practicing governance, not automation.
Design task-routing and working-group structures agents can coordinate between board meetings, using the DAO's zones as a template.
Define measurable outcomes for one real program and agree on what the Progress Tracker role reports and how often.
Close with an evidence brief built only from the world's verified map facts and cited sources, modeling disciplined information habits for staff.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized governance patterns (which decision types boards reserve to humans) and redacted outcome-metric templates, aggregated across cohorts to strengthen shared governance playbooks.
programs.consent: Organizational consent at registration plus individual opt-in; all shared material anonymized and reviewed before release; participants may request removal of any contribution; no donor, client, or financial data is ever shared.
